nodes.statement: Rewrite stochastic success measure as expectation of learner loss minus minimum expected fixed-comparator loss.
Remove distributional assumption; consider arbitrary y sequence; deterministic algorithm removes stochastic expectation.
Pathwise squared regret against the best single choice in hindsight; winning means sublinear growth.
V subset R^d, predictions, real losses, arbitrary u; general comparator regret.
Algorithm does not know u or its regret; no-regret defined by every fixed u and printed lim Regret_T(u)/T <=0.
Regret also depends on all losses, suppressed in notation.
Adversary may choose number after observing our choice and may act arbitrarily/adversarially.
Best hindsight constant equals empirical mean.
Cannot use final leader before future is known; track slowly changing past-optimal guess.
Strict-past empirical mean for t>=2; arbitrary first guess in [0,1]; definition/name FTL.
General Be-the-Leader inequality with assumed prefix minimizers.
Induction on T; base l_1(xStar_1)<=l_1(xStar_1).
For T>=2 assume prefix T-1 inequality and aim for T inequality.
Cancel the identical T-th terms to obtain (1.3).
Prefix online-leader losses <= prefix loss at xStar_(T-1).
Prefix loss at xStar_(T-1) <= prefix loss at xStar_T by minimization and membership.
Transitivity yields (1.3) and concludes inductive step.
Arbitrary bounded outcomes, x_1=0.5, strict-past means, R_T<=4+4 ln T.
Step areas for harmonic sum bounded using reciprocal integral.
Invoke BTL to upper bound regret.
Replace actual x_t by xStar_(t-1), minimum by cumulative loss at xStar_T.
R_T <= sum_t[(xStar_(t-1)-y_t)^2-(xStar_t-y_t)^2].
Initial excess <=0.5^2.
Expand squares and factor as (a+b-2y)(a-b).
Product <= |a+b-2y||a-b| <= 2|a-b|.
Substitute strict-past and current empirical means.
Separate y_t and combine coefficients 1/(t-1)-1/t.
Triangle inequality gives 2|sum_(i<t)y_i/[t(t-1)]|+2|y_t|/t.
Bound prefix sum and y_t to obtain <=2/t+2|y_t|/t<=4/t.
Integral comparison discussion begins; completes on printed p6.
Outcome/prediction in [0,1], reveal after prediction, squared loss.
Population mean predicts optimally; expected benchmark sigma^2*T; expected excess nonnegative.
H_T<=1+integral_2^(T+1) 1/(t-1) dt=1+ln T.
Conclude theorem by combining harmonic estimate and regret bound.
For positive t and y_i in [0,1], their empirical mean belongs to [0,1].
nodes.source_evidence: No explicit proof is given. The bounded average assertion is implicit in identifying mean as interval argmin.

nodes.statement: Positive-prefix empirical mean attains the interval squared-loss minimum. A full scalar-argmin library characterization also requires uniqueness, which is not separately stated as a printed theorem.
nodes.source_evidence: The source says the argmin equality should be immediate but provides no derivation. It uses scalar argmin notation without a separate uniqueness statement or argument.
nodes.closure: An independently proved complete minimizer characterization is required for a characterized library definition. Variance decomposition is a possible derived proof, not a printed source node.

nodes.statement: Under p1 i.i.d. bounded distribution, population mean minimizes expected squared loss and minimum cumulative expected fixed loss is T times variance.
nodes.source_evidence: p1 asserts optimality and value without deriving the squared-loss decomposition.
nodes.closure: Context-only source gap; does not feed the deterministic Theorem1.3 route.

routes.premise_discharge: i.i.d. bounded distribution belongs only to motivational expected-loss context.
Definition change: arbitrary realized outcomes and deterministic rule. This is not a theorem commuting min and E.
T>=1 and every y_i in [0,1]. The two source gaps remain open.
Only positive prefixes t-1 for t>=2; first value chosen separately in [0,1].
Inductive hypothesis invoked only at prefix T-1, T>=2.
Direct source lemma hypotheses: xStar_(T-1) minimizes prefix cumulative loss and xStar_T belongs to V.
Both inequalities are necessary for transitivity; cancellation recovers the full T inequality.
Induction schema discharges local IH in N-BTL-IH; this local assumption is not a new global theorem premise.
Theorem-local rule x_t=xStar_(t-1), including xStar_0=1/2. Mean characterization discharges minimum attainment.
Instantiate V=[0,1], l_t(u)=(u-y_t)^2, leaders empirical means. Mean gap supplies all prefix minimizer and membership obligations; they cannot be extra theorem binders.
Subtract BTL inequality in the correct direction from learner cumulative loss; distribute sum subtraction.
Theorem-local xStar_0=1/2, xStar_1=y_1, y_1 in [0,1]; no arbitrary initial-value generalization.
Real ring expansion for t>=2; a=xStar_(t-1), b=xStar_t.
a,b,y_t in [0,1] entail |a+b-2y_t|<=2; absolute values are nonnegative.
Positive prefix lengths t-1 and t; empirical-mean formula is applicable.
Split sum_(i<=t) at y_t; denominators nonzero because t>=2.
Use 1/(t-1)-1/t=1/[t(t-1)], triangle inequality, and t positive.
For i<t, 0<=y_i<=1, so |sum_(i<t)y_i|<=t-1; |y_t|<=1. These are source-used elementary interval side conditions.
Split sum into initial term and t=2,...,T; T>=1. Tail empty at T=1. Both initial and tail estimates are required.
Use 1/4<=4 and first harmonic term 1; T>=1.
Figure is explanatory evidence for geometric comparison, not a separate algebraic proof route.
Reciprocal shifted curve bounds bars for terms t>=2; separate first term 1. Integrate from2 toT+1 to get ln T. T>=1 includes zero-length integral at T=1.
Multiply H_T<=1+ln T by positive 4, combine transitivity, expand 4(1+ln T).
